_comment: Crisp conifers (ProceduralTreeExpansionPlan Increment A). Heights 1 cube=1 m, GAME-COMPRESSED for render density (the engine's #1 open issue) + legibility at typical camera distance — same compression the rest of this library uses for oak/spruce. Pine models Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris); USFS Silvics field heights ~13.7-29 m. pine_l=18 is INSIDE that range; pine_s=10 and pine_m=12 are BELOW the cited range floor (13.7 m) — deliberately shortened past what the real data supports, for a small/medium game asset, NOT a claim they're real young-stand heights. Fir models balsam fir (Abies balsamea); USFS Silvics 'heights range 12-18 m' verbatim, so fir_m=14 (mid) and fir_l=18 (top of range) both sit IN it. fullness:1.0 = solid crown so emit compresses interiors to whole cubes (cheap greedy faces) not holey subcubes. Sources: research.fs.usda.gov/silvics scotch-pine + balsam-fir.
Fullness axis (extremeness): height + fullness variants biomes weight toward a vibe. lush = tall + dense canopy; sparse = short + see-through.

Megaflora (ProceduralTreeExpansionPlan Increment B) — enchanted-forest giants, 1 cube = 1 m, CUBE resolution (mesher greedy-merges/culls interiors; sub/micro shells would blow the face count). Canopy radius capped at 24 cubes = the engine flora-margin ceiling (ObjectTemplateManager kFloraMarginCap) beyond which a canopy clips at chunk seams. redwood models coast redwood (Sequoia sempervirens); tallest living ~115.55 m (Hyperion, Sillett 2006 per Wikipedia), so xl=115 approaches that; redwood_l=90 is an interpolated old-growth size (no single named specimen). elder_oak is a fantasy world-tree with a sequoia-SCALE TRUNK (dia factor 0.13 ≈ General Sherman's real 11.1/83.8 = 0.1325, NPS) but a DELIBERATELY BROADENED crown (~1.6x Sherman's real crown ratio) for a spreading world-tree look — glowing root veins for the enchanted read.

Enchanted-forest glowing understory (Increment B/C). bush archetype with an emissive leaf material override (glow_green/glow_blue exist in materials.json). Paired with sparse giants (elder_oak/redwood) in the EnchantedForest biome's two-layer flora.
